review_evidence: README identifies a collection of formalized conjecture statements in Lean using mathlib, explicitly intended as an open benchmark for verified mathematical discovery.
The project organizes formal conjectures by source and also contains FormalConjecturesForMathlib definitions needed to state problems not yet expressible in released mathlib.

With 1,485 primary files, the formal statements and supporting definitions are exactly the sort of searchable formal prior art the corpus is intended to preserve, regardless of whether conjectures have proofs.
summary: Retain formal-conjectures as a large curated corpus of formal mathematical conjecture statements and supporting definitions.

review_evidence: find . -name '*.lean' | wc -l on the hydrated checkout: 1662 total .lean files, 197 more than this unit's 1465, i.e. already covered by a prior review snapshot.

grep -LE 'theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom|elab' over exactly the 1465 in-scope files: 12 hits with none of these keywords: FormalConjecturesUtil.lean, FormalConjecturesForMathlib.lean, FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/{MinimalOverlapProblem,HerzogSchonheimConjecture,HadwigerNelson,HappyEndingProblem,NoThreeInLineProblem,OddWeirdNumber,BrocardProblem,ErdosRadoSunflowerConjecture}.lean, FormalConjectures/GreensOpenProblems/{63,81}.lean. Read all 12 in full.

FormalConjecturesUtil.lean (1801 bytes) and FormalConjecturesForMathlib.lean (15898 bytes) are pure import lists: only a copyright header, `module`, and `public import`/`public meta import` lines -- no open, notation, attribute, or declaration. Verified prover-aware per FILTER-007: this makes them navigation-only, which FILTER-007 explicitly routes to ranking (FD-016, downranked but still indexed and queryable), not to hard exclusion; excluding them would remove queryable navigation the policy says must stay primary-eligible absent an end-to-end-verified auxiliary channel, which this review cannot establish.

The 10 Wikipedia/GreensOpenProblems files are one-screen pointer files: each has a copyright header, imports FormalConjecturesUtil plus one canonical FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«N» (or GreensOpenProblems.«N») module, a module docstring naming and describing the problem in prose (e.g. HadwigerNelson.lean: 'The Hadwiger-Nelson problem asks for the minimum number of colors...'), and a trailing `@[expose] public section` with no declarations after it. Read all 10 in full: none contains a theorem, def, notation, or attribute of its own.

These 10 hold unique searchable prose (the Wikipedia/common problem name and description) not duplicated verbatim in the canonical file they point to, so they do not satisfy FILTER-004's option 2 (exact duplicate with provenance alias); and per FILTER-007 the common name in the path/docstring is exactly the phrase a user is likely to search for even when the canonical declaration uses obscure internal numbering (e.g. Erdos508), so removing them would remove real navigation value, not just redundant text.

Checked file-size extremes across all 1465 files by sorting wc -c output. Smallest: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/OddWeirdNumber.lean (857, one of the 12 above). Read three other small files not flagged by the grep -- FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/196.lean (1010), FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/LehmerTotient.lean, FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/WoodalPrimes.lean -- each holds a real `theorem ... := by sorry` conjecture statement, confirming the grep is not missing declarations by a syntax quirk.

Largest: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/SidorenkoConjecture.lean (46428 bytes, 36 declaration-keyword matches) -- read the first 60 lines: full bibliographic references and a substantive statement of Sidorenko's conjecture in terms of homomorphism density, not a data dump.

Read the two named outliers flagged during the initial listing: scripts/extract_names.lean (16302 bytes, outside the FormalConjectures* tree) is a human-authored Lean program (structure TheoremInfo, several def/instance declarations, doc comments) that extracts corpus metadata from compiled .olean files -- real Lean declarations, not excluded on path alone per FILTER-002. FormalConjectures/WrittenOnTheWallII/Test.lean (22992 bytes) holds 50 real `theorem` declarations with tactic proofs (some ending `sorry`) computing graph invariants (independence number, domination number, Wiener index, etc.) on five named test graphs -- genuine formalized results, not a stub.

Read FormalConjecturesUtil/DeclName.lean, which the first grep pass (without 'elab' in the keyword set) had also flagged: it defines the `decl_name%` term elaborator via `open Lean Elab Term in elab ... => do ...`, a real declaration outside the theorem/def/structure/... keyword set, so it was excluded from the no-declaration count once 'elab' was added to the grep and is retained.

Read six more of the 20 initial grep hits that turned out to hold attribute/notation declarations once inspected: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/{SetTheory/Cardinal/Continuum,Analysis/Real/Cardinality,Data/Nat/Prime/Defs}.lean each add an `attribute [simp] ...` to an existing Mathlib lemma; FormalConjecturesForMathlib/{Geometry/Euclidean,Analysis/Asymptotics/Basic,NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/Basic}.lean each declare a `notation`/`scoped notation`. All six hold a genuine interface addition and are retained.

Read FormalConjecturesTest/Util/Linters/ModuleDocstringLinterImport.lean (1476 bytes): contains `#guard_msgs` test assertions and `set_option` exercising the module-docstring linter's duplicate-docstring warning -- real, human-authored test content, retained.
